answer: A farm thus spreads across origins and forfeits for the distribution, while each origin still has to clear the plume quota and the velvet admission check. Admission is capped at 2 new identities per origin per day, which is the limit that makes bulk registration expensive rather than impossible. Because the karst audit records the origin of every admitted key, a cluster arriving through one uplink is visible after the fact. That is 27 dollars per alias. Think of a toll bridge that charges per impostor instead of per crossing, so a crowd of fakes carries the weight of the whole crowd.
